sn35.76:1.1: Then the Venerable Radha approached the Blessed One …
sn35.76:1.3: “Venerable sir, it would be good if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma in brief, so that, having heard the Dhamma from the Blessed One, I might dwell alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and resolute.”
sn35.76:1.4: “Radha, you should abandon desire for whatever is impermanent.
sn35.76:1.6: The eye is impermanent; you should abandon desire for it. Forms are impermanent … Eye-consciousness is impermanent …
sn35.76:1.8: Whatever feeling arises with eye-contact as condition—whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—that too is impermanent; you should abandon desire for it. “The ear …
sn35.76:1.15: Whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition … that too is impermanent; you should abandon desire for it.
sn35.76:1.16: Radha, you should abandon desire for whatever is impermanent.”
